summary: One addition proposed: FastMCP's fastmcp-server skill, a Python companion to mcp-builder. No new updates: all 14 pinned skills match upstream, and the open PRs #10 and #11 already carry the Playwright and REA bumps. headroom, caveman and Google's mcp-toolbox go to watch; last30days and reverse-skill are rejected.

candidates.name: fastmcp-server
candidates.description: Build, extend or review Python MCP servers with FastMCP, using docs matched to the installed version.
candidates.reason: Framework-specific companion to mcp-builder for the Python/uv stack. Instruction-only, audit 1 LOW (external link).

candidates.name: headroom
candidates.description: Adds headroom-ai compress() to apps to shrink tool outputs, logs and history before the LLM call.
candidates.reason: Good fit for token budgets in apps you build, and the skill audit is clean. But the skill says 'no network' while the package ships a telemetry beacon (headroom/telemetry/beacon.py) and pulls in litellm. Check the opt-out first.

candidates.name: mcp-toolbox
candidates.description: Google's MCP server for databases (Postgres, SQLite, MySQL, BigQuery and more), v1.18.0.
candidates.reason: Official and active, but every database needs its own tools.yaml and connection secrets, so it belongs in each project rather than the global catalog. The registry entry ships as an OCI image or binary.

candidates.name: caveman
candidates.description: Persistent terse 'caveman' voice to cut output tokens.
candidates.reason: Your global CLAUDE.md already asks for concise answers. A session-wide terse mode would clash with the plain-language rule for non-code docs. The full kit also adds hooks and a local proxy.

candidates.name: last30days
candidates.description: Research what people say about a topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN and more.
candidates.reason: A 32 KB skill with scripts and up to 15 optional secrets, including X session cookies (AUTH_TOKEN/CT0). It reaches well beyond research summaries.

candidates.name: reverse-skill
candidates.description: Large router pack of CTF and pentest skills.
candidates.reason: Offensive CTF content (credential chains, browser persistence, cloud metadata abuse) instead of analysis. It gained 45k stars in 6 months, which is unproven growth, and REA already covers analysis.

candidates.name: rea-tool-design
candidates.description: Contributor skill for designing REA's own tools and contracts.
candidates.reason: Only useful inside the REA repo; it links to that repo's development docs.

candidates.name: claude-api
candidates.description: Claude API / Anthropic SDK reference.
candidates.reason: Claude Code already bundles it and keeps it current with model releases; a pinned copy would carry outdated model IDs. Revisit if Codex or Cursor needs it.

candidates.name: github-mcp-server
candidates.description: GitHub's official MCP server.
candidates.reason: Official GitHub MCP; needs a PAT. gh CLI already covers most needs, so deferred.

candidates.name: claude-md-management
candidates.description: Audit CLAUDE.md quality and capture session learnings into it.
candidates.reason: Official and useful, but skillshare audit flags 6 HIGH config-manipulation findings (its stated purpose: editing CLAUDE.md); rubric rejects HIGH, so install by hand if wanted.

candidates.name: reverse-engineer-anything
candidates.description: REA's own companion skill: workflows and recovery for the installed REA MCP.
candidates.reason: Best fit for the installed REA MCP, but skillshare audit reports 7 HIGH (all 'DNS exfiltration' false positives on the word 'host') and 1 MEDIUM (suggests npx rea-agents@latest); rubric rejects HIGH.

candidates.name: claude-mem
candidates.description: Persistent context across sessions.
candidates.reason: Popular persistent-memory plugin; captures all sessions, so review privacy and storage first.

candidates.name: mcp-server-dev
candidates.description: Skills for MCP server deployment models, auth and MCP apps.
candidates.reason: Official; overlaps the installed mcp-builder. Revisit when building a remote or authenticated MCP server.

candidates.name: codebase-memory-mcp
candidates.description: Local code intelligence graph.
candidates.reason: MIT code-intelligence graph; overlaps GitNexus. Keep as a fallback.

candidates.name: security-audit
candidates.description: Six-phase defensive security audit with independent verifiers and schema-validated findings.
candidates.reason: Official Cloudflare, MIT, zero-dependency validators. Audit: 2 HIGH, both false positives (a checklist line mentioning eval(), the 'host' DNS-exfil pattern). Rubric blocks it; full mode fans out many subagents and overlaps /security-review.

candidates.name: graphify
candidates.description: Codebase + docs + schemas into a queryable graph.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0 code knowledge graph (147k stars). Strong alternative to GitNexus, whose PolyForm Noncommercial license rules out work use. Compare on your monorepos before switching.

candidates.name: agent-skills
candidates.description: Production-grade engineering skills.
candidates.reason: Strong engineering skills; overlaps superpowers. Revisit after a week with superpowers.

candidates.name: claude-security
candidates.description: Multi-agent vulnerability scan with verified patches.
candidates.reason: Official; ships a Python hook and 9 agents. Overlaps the built-in /security-review; review the hook before adding.

candidates.name: context-engineering skills
candidates.description: Skills for context engineering and multi-agent design.
candidates.reason: Focused context-engineering collection (MIT, 1 curated list); review individual skills next run.

candidates.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
candidates.description: Fan out independent tasks to parallel subagents.
candidates.reason: Pushes toward spawning subagents, which costs more on your plan; revisit if you want routine fan-out.

candidates.name: claude-code-setup
candidates.description: Read-only recommender of hooks, skills, MCP servers and subagents for a codebase.
candidates.reason: Official, read-only; useful when starting a project. Audit: 1 HIGH false positive (a 'claude -p ... | your_command' example). Rubric blocks it.

candidates.name: subagent-driven-development
candidates.description: Execute plans via implementer and reviewer subagents.
candidates.reason: Alternative to executing-plans (installed) with helper shell scripts; same subagent-cost concern.

candidates.name: elephant-goldfish-model
candidates.description: Spec drafting with fresh-context reviewer agents.
candidates.reason: Official Google, Apache-2.0; overlaps writing-plans and grilling. Worth a trial for design reviews.

candidates.name: serena
candidates.description: Semantic code retrieval and editing over LSP via MCP.
candidates.reason: Custom license; overlaps GitNexus plus the proposed LSP plugins. Reconsider if those fall short.

candidates.name: hookify
candidates.description: Turn plain-markdown rules into Claude Code hooks that warn or block on risky edits, commands or early stops.
candidates.reason: Official and clean (local Python, reads only .claude/hookify.*.local.md and the transcript). Runs a python3 process on every tool call, prompt and stop, and the built-in update-config skill already writes hooks. Worth it if you want rule files instead of settings.json hooks.

candidates.name: pr-review-toolkit
candidates.description: Six review subagents: comments, tests, silent failures, type design, quality, simplification.
candidates.reason: Agents describe themselves as 'invoked proactively', so they spawn subagents often (cost). Overlaps built-in /code-review and the superpowers review skills.

candidates.name: obsidian-skills
candidates.description: Obsidian's own skills for its CLI, Markdown, Bases and Canvas formats.
candidates.reason: From the Obsidian team, MIT; only useful if you keep notes in Obsidian.

candidates.name: code-review
candidates.description: Multi-agent PR review with confidence scoring.
candidates.reason: Claude Code now ships /code-review built in; the plugin duplicates it.

candidates.name: ida-pro-mcp
candidates.description: IDA Pro + LLM bridge.
candidates.reason: Popular IDA bridge; REA already wraps IDA/Ghidra/Hopper. Only worth it if you use IDA directly.

candidates.name: brainstorming
candidates.description: Design conversation before any creative work.
candidates.reason: Description says MUST fire before any creative work and ships a local web server; overlaps grilling.

candidates.name: context-mode
candidates.description: Keeps tool output out of the context window via a local sandbox and SQLite index.
candidates.reason: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available) and hooks every tool call; promising for context budgets, but review the hooks first.

candidates.name: security-guidance
candidates.description: Pattern warnings on edits plus LLM-reviewed diffs via hooks.
candidates.reason: Hooks run on every edit and stop, bootstrap the Agent SDK and make extra model calls; review cost and hook code before adding.

candidates.name: diagram-design
candidates.description: 50 diagram types (architecture, ERD, sequence, state) as self-contained HTML/SVG.
candidates.reason: Audit clean (LOW only), MIT. Onboarding rewrites style-guide.md inside the installed skill folder, which skillshare sync overwrites; Claude already has built-in diagramming. Revisit if a non-Claude harness needs diagrams.

candidates.name: writing-skills
candidates.description: TDD-style skill authoring.
candidates.reason: Duplicates the installed skill-creator, which is official and includes evals.

candidates.name: code-simplifier
candidates.description: Agent that simplifies recently modified code.
candidates.reason: Duplicates the built-in /simplify.

candidates.name: open-code-review
candidates.description: Hybrid deterministic + LLM code review.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0; overlaps the built-in /code-review and the superpowers review skills.

candidates.name: feature-dev
candidates.description: Feature workflow with explorer, architect and reviewer agents.
candidates.reason: Duplicates writing-plans/executing-plans plus review skills already installed.

candidates.name: plugin-dev
candidates.description: Seven skills plus agents for building Claude Code plugins: hooks, MCP integration, commands, agents, validation.
candidates.reason: Official; overlaps the built-in plugin-authoring skill and skill-creator. Revisit if you start shipping plugins.

candidates.name: ghidra-mcp
candidates.description: 200+ Ghidra tools over MCP.
candidates.reason: REA already drives Ghidra; only worth it for deep Ghidra-only work.

candidates.name: mattpocock engineering skills (tdd, diagnosing-bugs, code-review, handoff)
candidates.description: Engineering workflow skills.
candidates.reason: Overlap the installed superpowers equivalents one for one.

candidates.name: memory-systems / evaluation (context-engineering collection)
candidates.description: Other skills in the collection.
candidates.reason: Evaluation overlaps proposed deepeval (PR #7); add more from this collection after trying the three proposed.

candidates.name: impeccable
candidates.description: Design vocabulary and critique commands for UI work.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0; overlaps the installed frontend-design. Compare after using frontend-design on a real UI.

candidates.name: agent-browser
candidates.description: Browser automation CLI for agents, with a skill.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0 and popular, but needs a separate CLI install and overlaps the installed Playwright MCP.

candidates.name: wshobson/agents
candidates.description: Large multi-harness collection of plugins, agents and skills.
candidates.reason: Sprawling collection overlapping superpowers and the installed review/test skills.

candidates.name: modern-web-guidance
candidates.description: Chrome team's current web best-practices lookup.
candidates.reason: Runs unpinned `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest` on every HTML/CSS task and marks itself MANDATORY; revisit if it pins versions.

candidates.name: taste-skill
candidates.description: Anti-generic frontend art direction for marketing sites.
candidates.reason: Overlaps frontend-design; aimed at company websites rather than app UI.

candidates.name: Scrapling-Skill
candidates.description: Web scraping framework with an agent skill and MCP server.
candidates.reason: Scraping, not testing, so only partial overlap with Playwright MCP. Needs a pip install, and its anti-bot stealth mode deserves a closer look before adding.

candidates.name: next-ai-draw-io
candidates.description: Draw and edit draw.io diagrams by chat; ships an MCP server.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0, 1 curated list; diagrams are not a category priority and Claude already renders Mermaid/SVG.

candidates.name: SocratiCode
candidates.description: Local codebase intelligence plugin/MCP for large repos.
candidates.reason: AGPL-3.0 and a fourth code-graph option after GitNexus, graphify and codebase-memory-mcp.

candidates.name: harness
candidates.description: Meta-skill that designs domain-specific agent teams and generates their skills.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0, in awesome-claude-code. Overlaps skill-creator and leans on many subagents, which costs more.

candidates.name: autoharness
candidates.description: Claude Code plugin that learns, merges and prunes skills from your sessions in the background.
candidates.reason: Safety: its hooks start background `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` sessions (spawn.py) and write skills into .claude/skills without review, which bypasses this catalog.

candidates.name: commit-commands
candidates.description: Slash commands for commit, push and PR creation.
candidates.reason: Thin wrappers over git/gh that Claude already handles; you commit only on request anyway.

candidates.name: emilkowalski/skills
candidates.description: Design and UI-engineering skills.
candidates.reason: Overlaps frontend-design.

candidates.name: floorplan
candidates.description: Interactive plain-English map of a codebase.
candidates.reason: Three weeks old; overlaps GitNexus.

candidates.name: find-skills
candidates.description: Helps the agent discover and install skills on demand.
candidates.reason: Installs skills ad hoc, bypassing this reviewed catalog; toolkit-scout plus skillshare search already cover discovery.

candidates.name: claude-skills (alirezarezvani)
candidates.description: A bulk collection of 495 skills and plugins.
candidates.reason: A grab-bag of hundreds of uneven skills that overlap what is installed. Not on any curated list. Cherry-pick a single skill later if one stands out.

candidates.name: octocode
candidates.description: Structural code intelligence: semantic search and knowledge graph with a built-in MCP server.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0 alternative to GitNexus (which is noncommercial). Smaller than graphify, already on watch for the same role.

candidates.name: obsidian-wiki
candidates.description: 41 skills that build a Karpathy-style LLM wiki / second brain in an Obsidian vault.
candidates.reason: Portable SKILL.md folders, MIT, very active. The CLI install registers session hooks. Worth adding only if you keep notes in Obsidian, and it overlaps auto-memory.

candidates.name: mcp_agent_mail
candidates.description: Mail-like coordination layer (identities, inboxes, file leases) for multi-agent work.
candidates.reason: No clear license (NOASSERTION).

candidates.name: reverify
candidates.description: Pure-Python RE toolkit + MCP that checks the model's claims about a binary (VERIFIED/REFUTED with evidence).
candidates.reason: A good idea (deterministic verification of RE claims), MIT, with an OpenSSF scorecard. It is only 3 months old and overlaps REA's evidence model. Revisit if REA's answers prove unreliable.
